item.title: A 115-Year-Old Swiss Tradition Gave Me a New Perspective on Adventure
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source. (Refinement was skipped, so the body is an excerpt of the original.)

Standing on a snow-covered slope in Switzerland, I joined locals enthusiastically cheering “hopp, hopp, hopp” (Swiss German for “go”) as racers careened downhill on velogemels — wooden, brakeless bikes with sled-like runners instead of wheels. Whizzing past, one by one, competitors feebly attempted to control their speed by digging their heels into the frozen ground.

I had originally come to the Swiss Alps for the world-class skiing, but when I heard about the velogemels, I was eager to try one. As an adventure seeker, I’ll try almost any contraption that gets me down a mountain, and this one sounded stranger than most.

Delta fans, take note: You can get some serious bonus miles in the coming weeks by booking a cruise.

Indeed, Delta Cruises says this is the richest accelerated mileage offer it has run all year.

Meanwhile, you can earn even more Delta miles by taking advantage of this promotion and paying for your cruise with a Delta SkyMiles-branded credit card. More on that below.

Note that you must act fast to get the bonus miles. The accelerated Delta Cruises mileage offer is only available through Dec. 15. It applies to new bookings for cruises scheduled between now and Dec. 31, 2027.

Details of the bonus mile offer

The Delta Cruises bonus miles offer is available to customers who book any cabin on any of the cruise brands available through Delta Cruises.

These include all the major cruise brands, such as Royal Caribbean, Carnival Cruise Line, Norwegian Cruise Line, MSC Cruises and Princess Cruises, as well as many smaller ocean, expedition and river cruise lines.

Among the caveats: Bonus miles are earned per cabin and are awarded to only one passenger per cruise booking. In addition, to qualify, customers must book through the Delta Cruises program at cruises.delta.com.

Also, the number of miles that customers earn as part of the promotion is based on the total cruise purchase price excluding port charges, port expenses, travel protection, taxes and fees charged at the time of booking.

There is no limit to the number of miles a customer can earn under the promotion.

In addition:

item.title: When Your Winter Trip Has No Snow, Find Your Inner Daredevil Instead.
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source. (Refinement was skipped, so the body is an excerpt of the original.)

I’ve never understood the appeal of roller coasters or similar thrill rides. The stomach-dropping plunges and screaming passengers who stumble off, then immediately get back in the perpetually long line? No, thank you. I’ve tried enough of them throughout my life to know they’re just not my thing.

So imagine my surprise — or horror, or maybe a bit of both — when I found myself willingly, eagerly even, climbing into an Olympic bobsled, knowing I’d soon be barreling down an icy track at nearly 80 miles per hour, experiencing up to five times the force of gravity. Even more surprising? It turned out to be one of my favorite travel experiences to date.

It happened on a ski trip that barely involved skiing. An unusually warm, dry winter had left the mountains in rough shape, and I’d gone hoping to improve my mediocre technique. Instead, I came home with a new appreciation for the kind of thrill I’d spent most of my life avoiding.

Source: Matador Network | Published: 2026-11-20 17:29 UTC

item.title: Visulahti Wax Museum in Mikkeli, Finland
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source. (Refinement was skipped, so the body is an excerpt of the original.)

About

Rather than being an impressive, polished wax museum, the Visulahti Wax Museum has become famous for its awkward, outdated, and sometimes unintentionally hilarious figures.

The museum has something of a cult reputation in Finland. Its wax figures are famously questionable in quality: many look surprisingly inaccurate, while some remind you more of a horror movie setting. In 1983, the Wax Museum was established with serious intentions, but nowadays people visit it mainly for nostalgic reasons. You have to approach the museum with a good sense of humour.

The collection rarely gets updated, and the once-popular TV stars are now unfamiliar to the younger audience. The newest figurine is the Finnish president, whose resemblance – or the lack of it – has been widely discussed in the national news.

There are also international stars displayed at the museum, such as Elvis, the Beatles, and Santa Claus. At the end of the tour, a creepy version of Mickey Mouse sings to you with his friends, as you walk out of the building, wondering what you just experienced.

Know Before You Go

Wax Cabinet is open only during the summer season; see the current entry price on the website. Entry is also included with the Visulahti wristband, which gives you access to other activities in the area as well.
